newsitem.title: USA: Mobil begins production offshore Equatorial Guinea.
newsitem.headline: Mobil begins production offshore Equatorial Guinea.

text.p: Mobil Corp said Wednesday commercial oil production has begun from the Zafiro field on Block B located offshore Equatorial Guinea in West Africa less than 18 months after its discovery.

Production from the Zafiro-1 well started up at an initial flow rate of 7,000 barrels of oil a day (bpd) on August 25. By year-end, Mobil said, production from the field is expected to reach a gross rate of 40,000 bpd from eight subsea wells. Mobil is the operator and holds a 75 percent interest in Block B with United Meridian Corp holding the remaining 25 percent.

Zafiro's development speed can be credited to aggressive drilling in combination with the application of floating production, storage and offloading system technology and subsea production facilities, Mobil said.
It said total initial development costs are estimated at $133 million.
The company said five wells have been completed with flowlines installed. Three additional development wells will be drilled, completed and tied in prior to year end to meet the production target.
Mobil acquired an interest in Block B from United Meridian in May 1994 and became operator in January 1995 after completion of the first wildcat well.
The Zafiro oil accumulation was discovered in March 1995. Mobil noted the field was declared commercial in October 1995 and a fast-track development plan initiated.
